name: White Pines Campsites
summary: Set in the Litchfield Hills near Riverton and the West Branch Farmington River in Northern Connecticut, White Pines Campsites offers 30- and 50-amp RV sites alongside cabins and yurts for rigs up to 40–45 feet.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 40–45 ft (30- and 50-amp RV sites)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — paved Litchfield Hills approach via US-44 and CT-8 North to CT-183 / Sandy Brook Road and Old North Road, with rolling hills and wooded turns
scorecard.treeClearance: Tall white pine and hardwood forest; main entrance avenues are trimmed for Class As and fifth-wheels while interior wooded loops have tighter overhead branches
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Main Avenue & Open Recreation-Adjacent 50-Amp Sites (up to 40–45 ft)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Wooded Pine Loops & Pond-Side Sites (under 32 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From US-44 in Winsted, take CT-8 North into Colebrook, turn right onto CT-183 (Sandy Brook Road) toward Riverton, and follow Old North Road to 232 Old North Rd. If approaching from the east via CT-20 West through Riverton, cross the West Branch Farmington River onto CT-183 and connect to Old North Road—avoiding steep, narrow forest roads through Peoples State Forest and around Barkhamsted Reservoir.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps large RVs on the primary CT-8 and CT-183 corridors via Winsted and Riverton rather than steep Peoples State Forest backroads.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the front check-in parking area off Old North Road before entering the pine-lined interior loops.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when staging near the Old North Road check-in lot and backing into pine-lined pads.

content.overview: Large family campground in Barkhamsted, CT (minutes from Riverton, the West Branch Farmington River, and 35 minutes northwest of Hartford) featuring 30- and 50-amp RV sites, safari tents, yurts, cabins, large swimming pool, arcade room, pond recreation area, and hiking trails.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electronics from rural Litchfield Hills voltage fluctuations on 30- and 50-amp hookup pedestals.

content.loopC: Wider 50-amp sites along the primary entrance avenues with easier swing angles for Class As, fifth-wheels, and travel trailers up to 40–45 ft.
content.loopsAB: Shaded pine-forest pads suited for travel trailers, Class Cs, and pop-ups under 32 ft.

name: Gibson Hill Campground

scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — paved state highway approach via I-395 Exit 28 or US-6 onto CT-14 / CT-14A and Gibson Hill Road, with rolling rural town roads
scorecard.treeClearance: Mature New England oak and pine forest with historic stone walls; main RV avenues are cleared while back wooded pads have lower limbs
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Main Avenue & Open Field Full-Hookup Sites (up to 40–45 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-395 North or South, take Exit 28 (CT-14 / Plainfield-Sterling) east on CT-14 through Sterling center, or approach from Rhode Island via US-6 West to CT-14A West and Gibson Hill Road to 177 Gibson Hill Rd. Avoid narrow rural cut-throughs off Bailey Road or unpaved town lanes.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps large RVs on primary CT-14 and CT-14A state corridors rather than narrow Quiet Corner cut-throughs.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the front check-in parking area off Gibson Hill Road before entering the wooded interior loops.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when staging near the Gibson Hill Road check-in area and backing into wooded pads.

content.overview: 60-acre family-oriented campground in Sterling, CT (minutes from the RI border, Foxwoods and Mohegan Sun, and Mystic) offering full-hookup RV sites, seasonal and monthly stays, fishing pond, bonfire circle, live weekend entertainment, and historic stone-wall hiking trails.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electronics from rural Quiet Corner voltage drops on 30- and 50-amp hookup pedestals.

content.loopC: Open, wider-radius full-hookup RV sites near the central activity area suited for Class As, fifth-wheels, and travel trailers up to 40–45 ft.
content.loopsAB: Quieter wooded pads bordered by historic stone walls suited for travel trailers, Class Cs, and pop-ups under 32 ft.

name: River Bend Campground
summary: Nestled along the Moosup River in eastern Connecticut just off CT-14A near the Rhode Island border, River Bend Campground offers 30- and 50-amp full-hookup RV sites with straightforward I-395 Exit 32 access and nearby Moosup Valley State Park Trail connectivity.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 40+ ft (select 50-amp full-hookup sites; wooded/riverside back-ins vary by loop)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — paved state highway approach via CT-14A, transitioning onto local Pond Street into the main check-in lane

scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Wooded Moosup River Bank & 30-Amp Back-In Sites (under 30 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Take I-395 Exit 32 (Plainfield / Sterling) onto CT-14A East (Plainfield Pike) and travel approximately 5 miles east into Oneco. Turn onto Main Street / Pond Street following campground signage to 41 Pond St. CT-14A is a paved two-lane state route with standard highway clearances—watch the local turn onto Pond Street in Oneco village and avoid consumer GPS shortcuts via narrow rural Sterling or Foster backroads when towing long rigs.

recommendedGear.reason: Routes big rigs cleanly via I-395 Exit 32 and CT-14A without sending you down narrow Windham County backroads.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the front check-in and staging area off Pond Street before proceeding into the wooded river loops, as internal camp roads narrow near the riverbank.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps watch low branches, trees, and river-edge boundaries when backing into wooded sites.

content.overview: Family-oriented Modern America Campgrounds park set in a wooded bend along the Moosup River, offering 30- and 50-amp full-hookup RV sites, an outdoor swimming pool, on-site food trailer, basketball and volleyball courts, weekend bingo and family entertainment, and access to the Moosup Valley Rail Trail just one mile away.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electronics on 30A/50A hookups in wooded New England river valleys.

content.loopC: Level 50-amp full-hookup sites positioned in the wider, sunnier central section near the pool and activity fields, offering easier swing angles and cleaner sky access for larger Class As, Class Cs, and fifth-wheels.
content.loopsAB: Shaded woodland and riverside sites tucked along the Moosup River; best suited for travel trailers, Class Cs under 30 ft, and pop-ups due to mature tree cover and tighter back-in angles.

name: Lone Oak Campsites
summary: Set on 250 acres in the Berkshire foothills at the base of Canaan Mountain, Lone Oak Campsites features over 400 campsites with direct US-44 (Norfolk Road) access 3.5 miles east of Route 7 and full-hookup 30/50-amp pull-throughs alongside wooded mountain loops.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 45+ ft (50-Amp Full-Hookup Pull-Throughs; wooded back-in loops vary by terrain)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: High — wide highway frontage directly on US-44 (Norfolk Rd) with spacious registration pull-off lanes
scorecard.treeClearance: Open sky in lower meadow/pull-through sections; mature deciduous and pine canopy in upper Canaan Mountain loops requires roof/slide checks
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Wooded Hillside & Rustic Back-In Loops (under 30 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Approach directly via US-44 (Norfolk Road). If traveling east from the US-44 / Route 7 intersection in Canaan, the campground entrance is 3.5 miles ahead on your right. From the south or east (Hartford/I-84/CT-8), take CT-8 North to Winsted and head west on US-44 through Norfolk into East Canaan, where the entrance will be on your left. US-44 is a primary highway with standard commercial clearances, though the stretch west of Norfolk features rolling Berkshire grades—avoid narrow local backroads when towing large fifth-wheels or Class A motorhomes.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps big rigs routed strictly on US-44 and Route 7 rather than steep Berkshire hill cut-throughs.

toadStrategy.text: Guests on 50-amp pull-through sites can pull straight in without unhooking. For hillside back-in sites, unhook in the wide paved and gravel registration staging area immediately inside the US-44 entrance before navigating the wooded interior loops.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps watch tree trunks and terraced hillside rock walls when backing into wooded sites.

content.overview: Sprawling 250-acre Modern America Campgrounds resort at the base of Canaan Mountain offering 400+ sites (30/50-amp full hookups, water/electric, and rustic sites), two swimming pools, a hot tub, sports courts, Hayloft Lounge live entertainment, and weekend car shows and events.

recommendedGear.reason: Helpful for fine-tuning side-to-side leveling on terraced Berkshire foothill pads.

content.loopC: Level 50-amp full-hookup pull-through and open-field sites near the main recreation hub, built for Class A motorhomes, Super Cs, and large fifth-wheels with wide turn radii and clear sky exposure.
content.loopsAB: Shaded, terraced forest sites tucked against the foothills of Canaan Mountain; ideal for travel trailers, Class Cs under 30 ft, and pop-ups seeking privacy and tree cover.
